title: Early civilisations timeline strip
subject: History
unit: Spring 1: Early river civilisations and Shang China (Dynamic Dynasties)
source: Seeded from history/y5 lessons 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 (Early civilisations timeline strip (portal printable))
intro: To understand where and when the earliest civilisations began and why rivers mattered

questions.q: Which river did ancient Egypt grow beside?
questions.a: The Nile
questions.model: Look at the four rivers. Egypt matches the Nile. So the answer is the Nile.

questions.q: Which began first: Shang China or Sumer?
questions.a: Sumer (about 3500 BC)

questions.q: Give one reason rivers helped civilisations.
questions.a: For example: water for crops, fertile soil or trade

questions.q: Give one way the river helped the Shang.
questions.a: For example: fertile silt for crops
questions.model: Think: what do farmers need? Good soil. The river leaves fertile silt. So it helped them farm.

questions.q: Give one way the river harmed the Shang.
questions.a: Floods destroyed homes and crops

questions.q: What was the last Shang capital?
questions.a: Yin, near modern Anyang

questions.q: What does 'cast' mean?
questions.a: Pour hot liquid metal into a mould
questions.model: Read the keyword. Cast: pour melted metal into a mould. When it cools it takes the mould's shape.

questions.q: What does a huge bronze vessel tell us about the Shang?
questions.a: They were wealthy, organised and skilled

questions.q: Who usually owned bronzes?
questions.a: Kings and rich nobles

questions.q: What were oracle bones made from?
questions.a: Ox shoulder bones and turtle shells
questions.model: Read the first slide. They were bones and shells. Ox shoulder bones and turtle shells.

questions.q: Name one thing Shang kings asked about.
questions.a: For example: harvests, weather, war or illness

questions.q: When were oracle bones recognised as writing?
Write one similarity between Egypt and Shang China.
questions.a: For example: both grew beside a river that flooded
questions.model: Pick a row: River. Egypt: the Nile. Shang: the Yellow River. Both grew beside rivers that flooded and left fertile soil.

questions.q: Write one difference.
questions.a: For example: Egypt had pharaohs and pyramids; Shang had kings and bronzes

questions.q: When did the Shang end?
questions.a: About 1046 BC

questions.q: Core: Make a timeline of the four civilisations and label each river on a world map.
questions.a: Sumer about 3500 BC (Tigris and Euphrates); Egypt about 3100 BC (Nile); Indus about 2600 BC (Indus); Shang about 1600 BC (Yellow River)
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: line from 4000 BC to 1000 BC, mark 3500 BC 'Sumer', then find the Tigris on the map.

questions.q: Extend: Write a sentence explaining why the first cities grew by rivers.
questions.a: They had water, fertile soil for farming and a way to travel and trade

questions.q: Stretch: How many years after Sumer's first cities did the Shang dynasty begin?
Core: Make a 'friend or enemy' table for the Yellow River with three points each side.
questions.a: Friend: silt, water, fish/transport. Enemy: floods, changing course, lost crops
questions.model: Teacher shows row 1: 'Friend: leaves fertile silt. Enemy: floods destroy homes.'

questions.q: Extend: Write a paragraph answering the big question. Use the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: It was both. It gave fertile soil, but its floods destroyed homes, so the Shang had to manage it

questions.q: Stretch: How is the Yellow River like the Nile for Egypt?
questions.a: Both flooded and left fertile soil that let farming and cities grow

questions.q: Core: Draw and label the steps of casting a Shang bronze vessel (five steps).
questions.a: Clay model, clay mould, pour bronze, cool, break mould and polish
questions.model: Teacher shows step 1: a clay pot shape labelled 'make a clay model'.

questions.q: Extend: Write what bronze objects tell us about Shang society.
questions.a: Skilled workers, rich and powerful rulers, important ceremonies

questions.q: Stretch: Why are objects from tombs good evidence but not the whole story?
questions.a: They show rich people's lives, not ordinary farmers'

questions.q: Core: Write five facts about oracle bones in a fact file. Use the portal response box or your book.
questions.a: Made of ox bones and turtle shells; questions carved; heated to crack; earliest Chinese writing; found in 1899
questions.model: Teacher shows fact 1: 'Oracle bones were ox shoulder bones or turtle shells.'

questions.q: Extend: What do the questions tell us about Shang worries?
questions.a: They worried about food, weather, war and health

questions.q: Stretch: Why does Islam forbid fortune-telling, and how should a Muslim face worries instead?
questions.a: Only Allah knows the unseen; a Muslim makes du'a, plans wisely and trusts Allah

questions.q: Core: Write a comparison paragraph of Egypt and Shang China using 'both', 'but' and 'whereas'. Use the portal response box.
questions.a: For example: Both grew beside rivers. Egypt had pharaohs, whereas the Shang had kings. Both had writing, but in different scripts.
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: 'Both Egypt and Shang China grew beside great rivers that flooded and left fertile soil.'

questions.q: Extend: Add one sentence about each civilisation's legacy.
questions.a: For example: Egypt left the pyramids; the Shang left the beginnings of Chinese writing

questions.q: Stretch: Which legacy matters more today? Give a reason.
questions.a: For example: Chinese writing, because over a billion people still use characters that grew from it

questions.q: A dynasty is:
questions.a: A line of rulers from one family
options: A line of rulers from one family

questions.q: Big question: why did the first great civilisations all grow up beside rivers?
questions.a: Rivers gave water, fertile soil for food and routes for trade

questions.q: Silt is:
questions.a: Fine mud carried by a river
options: Fine mud carried by a river

questions.q: Big question: was the Yellow River a friend or an enemy to the Shang?
questions.a: Both: it brought fertile soil and water but also deadly floods

questions.q: An artefact is:
questions.a: An object made by people in the past
options: An object made by people in the past

questions.q: Big question: how do bronze objects help us understand the Shang?
questions.a: They show the Shang were skilled, organised and had rich, powerful rulers

questions.q: An inscription is:
questions.a: Writing cut into a hard surface
options: Writing cut into a hard surface

questions.q: Big question: what can 3,000-year-old bones tell us about the Shang?
questions.a: Their writing, their worries (harvests, war, weather) and how kings ruled

questions.q: A legacy is:
questions.a: What is left behind for the future
options: What is left behind for the future

questions.q: Big question: how were ancient Egypt and Shang China alike, and how were they different?
questions.a: Alike: river, rulers, writing, skilled crafts. Different: pharaohs and pyramids vs kings, bronzes and oracle bones
